name: The Singular Patagonia
positioning: Hotel-museum built in a former 1915 sheep-processing plant at Puerto Bories, on the Señoret Channel five minutes from Puerto Natales in Chilean Patagonia
best_for: Travelers who want a base for excursions to Torres del Paine National Park
Guests interested in industrial heritage and Patagonian history

facts.text: The hotel is in Chilean Patagonia, five minutes from Puerto Natales, on the Señoret Channel.
The Singular Patagonia was built on the site of the former Frigorífico Bories, which was declared a National Monument in 1996.
The main structures were built as a sheep-processing plant in 1915.
In the transition areas of the hotel-museum, the old machinery remains intact and visible.
The hotel's museum is open to the public and covers the history of Puerto Bories and the old cold-storage plant that gave rise to the hotel.
The hotel offers guests a guided tour of the history of the former cold-storage plant.
Excursions can start from the hotel to remote places, including Torres del Paine National Park.
The hotel sits alone on the waterfront with a dock dating back to the sheep-processing days.
The hotel provides bikes that guests can ride into Puerto Natales.
The restaurant menu uses Patagonian ingredients such as guanaco, king crab, rhubarb and austral hake, in a setting overlooking the austral fjords.
The Singular Restaurant's cuisine is by Executive Chef Hernán Basso, fusing French trends with locally sourced ingredients.

highlights.text: The pool is indoor/outdoor, letting guests swim under a giant window looking out onto the Sound and out into the open air.
Rooms feature a wall-sized window looking out onto Última Esperanza Sound, and all rooms have the same view.
A funicular takes guests down from the brick reception area to the main building.
Excursions offered include a 12-hour trek to the base of the Paine Massif, kayaking on the Sound and a cooking class with the executive chef.
The spa's sauna has a view of the Sound.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the remote Patagonian location requires significant travel planning.
WhataHotel notes outdoor activities and excursions depend on the weather.
The hotel stands alone on the waterfront outside Puerto Natales, so the town is a bike ride away.
